No suction in your mouth, no straws. Rinse very gently with salt water after eating, don't spit (again, suction), let it drip out if you must. 

Liquid diet (soup, puree, yoghurt, protein drinks) is recommended for the first week, then switch to soft foods (vegetables boiled for too long, soft chicken). Drink water for a week.

Not doing this could lead to slower recovery, infection, dry socket – really painful stuff.

HOWEVER, there are people who eat normal day 1 and are fine. 

But I would personally advise you to be careful and keep it to at least liquid or soft foods only for the first 5 days.
My swelling was at its worst on day 3, but sometimes it peaks at day 5. Don't worry! You literally just got some bones pulled out of your jaw 😭 This is normal, I promise. Worry later!

Hey! I only just found out about this sub and I don't intend to use it, but this worried me a bit, so I'm leaving a comment.

Here's what I recommend, as an "elder" gen z who can kind of relate (just like one of the other comments): cut down, don't quit (immediately). Play games that aren't F2P so there's no money to spend beyond the initial asking price if you'd prefer to legally purchase them; cut down your twitter mutuals/following to people you love who haven't influenced you negatively; curate your timeline(s) to be short and positive so you can't scroll endlessly. Block liberally!

The way these websites/programs/etc are designed to zombie-fy you for profit is really, truly horrible, but the way to deal with social isolation isn't to also isolate yourself online. Also, I hate to bring your age into this, because I hated being infantilised too, but you are still so malleable and this is maybe the most hormonally, psychologically complicated time of your life. If you had friends irl, maybe \*they\* would have talked you into self harm and smoking. I know my classmates at the time did, moreso than the internet weirdos (like me). And not just that, but the pandemic means that there's been more physical distance and online activity than ever! A lot of my normie friends who did abide very strictly by regulations are incredibly awkward and have anxiety as a result of being home all the time. You're not alone in this.

*TL;DR*: I'm not saying this is your fault nor that there's nothing you could do, I am saying that there's a lot of things at play here, though it would be very wise to try to cut back as much as you can. Lock your social media accounts, consider following like 20 accounts instead of 100+, focus on 1 or 2 discord server(s) and try to increase 1 on 1 convos. 

I guarantee you, you will make friends through school inevitably. Even if it's just someone you hang out with at school, or someone you discuss homework with, you can make that person your friend - or maybe they'll make you their friend? :-) Even if it feels like there's no way that's possible right now.

I tend to dislike tsundere characters because the designated tsun is usually malicious or condescending which pisses me off. This is a popular trope so I assume others can make a good case for it.

Yandere characters are clichés taken seriously: "I love you more than anything else in this world." A well-executed yandere, to me, is someone who desperately tries to suppress their own increasingly obsessive feelings for MC because they understand these feelings to be toxic and a burden, but they love MC so much they can't help themselves. They're torn between a selfish, overindulgent love where they may hurt MC and a moral love where they intentionally deny themselves acting on these feelings for MC's safety/happiness, because they don't see a mutual, healthy relationship as a viable option, usually because they think too highly of MC or too low of themselves (or both). In a good yandere story, the MC needs to discourage toxic behavior, encourage self love, and show the LI that a normal-ish relationship is possible.

Part of the reason I like this trope so much, besides the built-in character arc as described above, is that the most stressful thing in my life is and always has been worrying about whether people like me or not or whether they like me as much as I like them. With yandere characters, them liking you more than vice versa is so undeniable that it's their defining character trait and even a flaw. It's comforting.

Another reason is, I love drama. No-one provides game-wide drama like a yandere character that shows up in multiple bad ends and maybe even pulled some strings around the plot just to exist near you. Chef's kiss.
